answer: Latency Pigment Test. Each agent identity must show a stable inter-arrival timing signature ("pigment") across its first N transactions, and new identities may only harbor traffic whose autocorrelation matches that signature within tolerance. Enforcement is a rolling check: mismatched or jittered bursts throttle to one action per cycle. Attackers pay per-identity calibration cost—sustained pacing, unique timing noise, and marble-like consistency over weeks—making mass account creation linearly expensive in compute and maintenance.
